newsitem.title: USA: Private jet crashes at suburban Chicago field.
newsitem.headline: Private jet crashes at suburban Chicago field.

text.p: A small private jet crashed at an airport in this northwest Chicago suburb Wednesday, killing all four people on board, police said.
The accident occurred at Palwaukee Airport, a small general aviation field which handles corporate and commuter traffic.

Aon Corp, a Chicago-based insurance and financial services company, said Arthur Quern, 54, was on board and died in the crash. Quern served as chairman and chief executive of Aon Risk Services Companies Inc and senior vice president and corporate secretary for Aon Corp. Larry Koppie, 53, an Aon pilot, also died in the crash.
Alberto-Culver Co said it owned the plane but had no other information on the accident or the victims.

The Federal Aviation Administration said the Gulfstream-4 crashed on takeoff. Police said the plane hit an embankment as it came down, skidded across a road and came to rest in the parking lot of an apartment complex where it exploded and burned.
The plane wound up about 15 feet from the nearest building but no one on the ground was injured.
